_comment: Home Assistant versions of the whole-system timelines of the bridge (tests/spec/system_scenarios.json of tkislan/paradox), played by tests/scenarios.py against the integration and the fake panel of tests/fake_panel.py. Written in this repository, not copied from the bridge. Top level: _comment, login, and the groups startup, keep_alive, armed, sensors, commands and setup_failures, each a list of rows. Each row is one scenario: the config entry is set up, then 'steps' are played in order. 'login' is copied from the bridge file: the config entry logs in with username and password, and the panel hands out session and accepts u and p for it. Before a row's panel keys apply, the panel has require_login on, the six default zones Predsien, Lava izba, Prava izba, Spalna, Obyvacka, Chodba, a statuszone of 32 zeros, useraccess [1, 0] and no alarms or troubles. Row keys: name, ported_from (the bridge row it ports, as '<bridge group>/<bridge row name>'), note? (how the port differs from the bridge row), panel?, setup, steps?. panel: zones ([area bitmask, name] pairs, padded to 32 slots with unused [0, ' ']), statuszone and useraccess (lists of zone status and area state codes), alarms and troubles (lists of index strings, which the panel writes quoted), accept_login (false: no login is accepted), default_page (the page that answers accepted credentials, an inline string or {file: path relative to tests/}; the captured default page when omitted), down (true: every request is answered with a reset connection), faults (a list of faults, active from the start). A fault is {path, kind, times?}: the next 'times' requests for path (whatever their query), all of them when times is omitted, fail as kind: http_500 (HTTP 500), reset (connection closed before any response), hang (never answered), login_page (status 200 with the login page), garbage (status 200 with a page that has neither a session value nor status tables), wrong_title (status 200 with a page titled 'Other'), or page ({path, kind: 'page', page, times?}: status 200 with 'page', an inline string or {file}). aiohttp sends a GET again, once, when its connection is closed before any response, so every reset request reaches the panel twice: a fault that resets N requests of the integration has times 2N, and the request lists hold each of them twice. setup is {advance_s?, expect}: the config entry is set up; with advance_s, the setup runs while the clock moves on that many seconds, and must be over by then. Step keys, applied in this order: panel_status ({statuszone?, useraccess?, alarms?, troubles?} the panel serves from now on), panel_zones (the zones the index page serves from now on), panel_fault (a fault), panel_expire_session (true: the panel drops the session), panel_down (the panel's down from now on), action ({service, area}: the alarm_control_panel service alarm_arm_away, alarm_arm_home, alarm_arm_night or alarm_disarm, called on the entity of the 0-based area and waited for), advance_s (the clock moves on this many seconds, one at a time, and each time every timer due within the next half second runs). expect describes the end of the setup or of a step and what happened during it: entry_state (loaded, setup_retry or setup_error), reauth_in_progress (whether a reauth flow for the entry is open), action_error (the translation key of the error the action raised), panel_requests (every request line the panel received, in order, as 'GET <path?query>'), panel_requests_any_order (the same, compared as a multiset, for timers due in the same second), panel_request_counts ({request line: count} of every request line received, for long stretches of time), states ({'zone_<slot>' | 'area_<index>': state}: the state of the entity whose unique ID ends that way, or 'absent' when there is none; entities left out are not checked). entry_state, reauth_in_progress and states are checked only when given. An expect has at most one of panel_requests, panel_requests_any_order and panel_request_counts; with none of them, no request is expected, and an absent action_error means that the action raised nothing. The integration's timing: the setup logs in and polls GET /statuslive.html once before any entity exists; after it, a poll follows every second and GET /keep_alive.html?msgid=1 every 3 seconds, counted from the end of the setup; an accepted action polls at once; a failed setup ends with GET /logout.html, after the client's own logout when the index page failed every attempt. Porting: the bridge's start becomes the setup, which also takes the bridge's first poll; advance_ms becomes advance_s, and the bridge's steps of 999 ms and 1 ms are joined into whole seconds; the armed topic becomes the state of area_0, and paradox/sensor/<slot> becomes zone_<slot>; a process exit becomes the entry state; failed commands become action_error; MQTT-only and log expectations and the requests a bridge row ignores are dropped.

startup.name: a panel with no zone in use starts and still reports the armed state
startup.ported_from: startup/a panel with no zone in use starts and still reports the armed state

startup.name: a failing logout before login is tolerated
startup.ported_from: startup/a failing logout before login is tolerated

startup.name: index page failures are retried and the setup still succeeds
startup.ported_from: startup/index page failures are retried 1000 ms apart and startup still succeeds
startup.note: The bridge's steps of 999, 1, 1000 and 1000 ms, which expect one index page request per second, are joined into the setup's 3 s, so the row checks that the retries end within 3 s; the client's own tests pin the 1000 ms between them.

startup.name: a successful login answered with a pretty-printed default page is recognised and the setup succeeds
startup.ported_from: startup/a successful login answered with a pretty-printed default page is recognised and startup succeeds

startup.name: with a zone name with a hyphen the setup succeeds and the zone is monitored
startup.ported_from: startup/a zone name with a hyphen starts the bridge and the zone is monitored

keep_alive.name: a keep-alive request GET /keep_alive.html?msgid=1 every 3 s
keep_alive.ported_from: keep_alive/a keep-alive request GET /keep_alive.html?msgid=1 every 3000 ms
keep_alive.note: The bridge's steps of 2999 ms and 1 ms become steps of 2 s and 1 s.

keep_alive.name: steady state: 30 s of an unchanged panel are 30 polls and 10 keep-alives, and the area is still disarmed
keep_alive.ported_from: keep_alive/steady state: 30 s of an unchanged panel are 30 polls, 10 keep-alives and a single message
keep_alive.note: The bridge's single message is the armed state of its first poll, which the setup takes here; how often Home Assistant writes a state is not checked.

keep_alive.name: a keep-alive answered with HTTP 500 is only logged
keep_alive.ported_from: keep_alive/a keep-alive answered with HTTP 500 is only logged

keep_alive.name: a keep-alive with a reset connection is only logged
keep_alive.ported_from: keep_alive/a keep-alive with a reset connection is only logged

keep_alive.name: a keep-alive answered with the login page is only logged
keep_alive.ported_from: keep_alive/a keep-alive answered with the login page is only logged

armed.name: armed panel: armed_away from the setup on, unchanged at the next poll
armed.ported_from: armed/armed panel: ON at the first poll, not repeated
armed.note: That the bridge does not repeat its message has no Home Assistant counterpart: how often Home Assistant writes a state is not checked.

armed.name: arming code 7 is arming
armed.note: The bridge counts code 7 as armed (ON); Home Assistant has an arming state of its own for it.

armed.name: disarmed to arming to armed_away to arming to disarmed: arming and armed_away are separate states
armed.ported_from: armed/disarmed to arming to armed to disarmed: arming and armed are one state
armed.note: The bridge publishes nothing while codes 7 and 2 alternate, as both are ON; Home Assistant changes state each time.

armed.name: an empty useraccess table gives no area entity, also once the area is armed
armed.ported_from: armed/an empty useraccess table is an unknown state
armed.note: An area gets its entity only when it is in use at setup, so area_0 stays absent where the bridge publishes ON.

armed.name: a useraccess table with a single entry is read as that entry
armed.ported_from: armed/a useraccess table with a single entry is read as that entry

armed.name: sleep, stay, entry delay and instant (4, 5, 6, 10) are armed_night, armed_home, pending and armed_home; ready and not ready (8, 9) are disarmed
armed.ported_from: armed/sleep, stay, entry delay and instant (4, 5, 6, 10) publish ON; ready and not ready (8, 9) publish OFF

armed.name: an area in alarm is triggered, and back to its own state once the alarm clears
armed.ported_from: armed/areas in alarm and active troubles publish nothing, neither when they appear nor when they clear
armed.note: The bridge publishes nothing for an area in alarm; Home Assistant shows it as triggered. The troubles are still served with the alarm, but have no Home Assistant expectation yet.

sensors.name: a sensor opening turns its own zone on and closing turns it off
sensors.ported_from: sensors/a sensor opening publishes ON on its own topic and closing publishes OFF

sensors.name: closed codes 0, 3, 5, 7 and 8 close an open sensor, open code 9 keeps it open
sensors.ported_from: sensors/closed codes 0, 3, 5, 7 and 8 close an open sensor, open code 9 keeps it open

sensors.name: one poll with several changes updates the area and every changed zone
sensors.ported_from: sensors/one poll with several changes publishes the armed state first, then sensors by ascending index
sensors.note: The order of the bridge's messages has no Home Assistant counterpart; the row checks the states after each poll.

sensors.name: status entries of unused slots have no zone entity
sensors.ported_from: sensors/status entries of unused slots are never published

sensors.name: a sensor that opens and closes between two polls is never seen
sensors.ported_from: sensors/a sensor that opens and closes between two polls is never seen

sensors.name: a status table shorter than the zone list reads missing entries as closed
sensors.ported_from: sensors/a status table shorter than the zone list reads missing entries as closed

sensors.name: a status table with a single entry is read as that entry
sensors.ported_from: sensors/a status table with a single entry is read as that entry

sensors.name: with no zone in use no zone entity ever exists
sensors.ported_from: sensors/with no zone in use no sensor is ever published

sensors.name: with 32 zones in use, zones past the 16th get entities and states too
sensors.ported_from: sensors/with 32 zones in use, zones past the 16th are published too

sensors.name: open codes 2, 4, 6 and 9 keep an open sensor open and open a closed one
sensors.ported_from: sensors/open codes 2, 4, 6 and 9 keep an open sensor open and open a closed one

sensors.ported_from: sensors/an unused slot in front has no sensor, and the zones after it publish on their own slot

sensors.name: an unused slot between zones has no zone entity, and the zone after it takes the state of its own slot
sensors.ported_from: sensors/an unused slot between zones has no sensor, and the zone after it publishes on its own slot

sensors.name: zones of area 2 and of both areas are monitored like those of area 1, each on its own slot
sensors.ported_from: sensors/zones of area 2 and of both areas are monitored like those of area 1, each on its own slot

commands.ported_from: mqtt_commands/arm command: panel is told to arm, the next poll publishes ON

commands.ported_from: mqtt_commands/disarm command: panel is told to disarm, the next poll publishes OFF

setup_failures.ported_from: failures/wrong panel credentials exit with code 1

setup_failures.ported_from: failures/an unreachable panel exits with code 1

setup_failures.ported_from: failures/a login page request failing with HTTP 500 exits with code 1

setup_failures.ported_from: failures/a default page with another title means login failed and exits with code 1

setup_failures.note: The bridge's steps of 999 ms, 1 ms and nine of 1000 ms, which expect one index page request per second, are joined into the setup's 10 s, so the row checks that the retries end within 10 s; the client's own tests pin the 1000 ms between them.
